question: When do classes start for the 2026-27 autumn term?
reference_answer: Classes for the Autumn Term (Term-I) of session 2026-27 start on Monday, July 27, 2026.

question: when is winter vacation this year
reference_answer: Winter vacation for students runs from Thursday, December 31, 2026 to Sunday, January 10, 2027.

question: Is Diwali a holiday in 2026 and on which date?
reference_answer: Yes. Diwali is on the 2026 holiday list on 8 November 2026, a Sunday.

question: How often is my mentor supposed to meet me?
reference_answer: A mentor meets every Category 1 mentee at least once a month, in a slot of at least half an hour booked in the Student Counseling Interface on UMS. A mentee can ask for more meetings by appointment.

question: Can I vape or use an e-cigarette on campus?
reference_answer: No. The smoke-free policy treats electronic smoking devices such as e-cigarettes as smoking, and smoking or using tobacco products is prohibited on all LPU facilities, property and vehicles.

question: Are the LPU buses air conditioned?
reference_answer: No. The transport facility uses non-AC buses only, except on the Ludhiana route.

question: After the end term exam can I see my answer sheet and ask for re-evaluation?
reference_answer: Yes. After every MTT and ETE, students can physically scrutinise their evaluated answer booklets, and a student who is not satisfied can apply online through UMS for re-evaluation.

question: Do I have to pay for a doctor's consultation at the Uni Health Centre?
reference_answer: No. OPD consultation is free; patients pay only for medicines and recommended tests. Medicines are sold at subsidised rates at the 24-hour chemist shop.

question: How much education loan can I get without collateral?
reference_answer: Through the university's NBFC partners, education loans of up to ₹30 lakh need no collateral, but a co-borrower is mandatory. Bank loans above ₹7.5 lakh may require collateral security.

question: a senior is ragging me, who do I complain to?
reference_answer: The aggrieved student or their parent or guardian reports the incident to the Anti-Ragging Squad, which enquires into it and sends its report and recommendations to the Anti-Ragging Committee.

question: If I'm not happy with the grievance committee's decision, who can I appeal to?
reference_answer: To the Ombudsperson, whom the university appoints to hear appeals against decisions of the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee, once all other remedies under the policy have been used. Appeals about revaluation or re-totalling of answer sheets are not heard.

question: What are the hostel charges for a 4 seater room in 2026-27?
reference_answer: For the full 2026-27 academic year, a 4-seater costs Rs 83,700 for an air-cooled standard room (300 free electricity units), Rs 92,700 for an air-conditioned standard room (500 units) and Rs 99,000 for an air-conditioned studio apartment (500 units).

question: Is parking free for students who live in the hostels?
reference_answer: Yes. Residential students get free parking, though the parking area may be some distance from their allotted accommodation.

question: How does an international student apply for a fee refund?
reference_answer: By sending the original refund form, filled in and signed by the student and the parent or guardian, by email to int.admissions@lpu.co.in by the last date of refund.

question: Is there a minimum attendance for each course or only an overall percentage?
reference_answer: Both. Students are expected to attend at least 80% of classes. After a 5% relaxation for medical and other genuine reasons, at least 75% aggregate attendance is mandatory, with at least 65% in each individual course.

question: What happens to my hostel room if I join a few days after the session starts?
reference_answer: If a student does not report within 3 days of the scheduled start of session, the room already allotted may be de-allocated. If late joining is permitted, a room may be allotted again subject to availability, but not necessarily of the same category or seater pattern.

question: What is the minimum and maximum duration of a PhD at LPU?
reference_answer: At least three years from the date of registration and at most six years, for both full-time and part-time scholars.

question: What marks do I need in my master's degree to apply for a PhD?
reference_answer: At least 55% aggregate marks (or an equivalent grade) in a relevant master's degree, plus qualifying LPUNEST and an interview. SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer), differently-abled and EWS candidates get a 5% relaxation.

question: I fractured my right hand before exams. Can someone write the paper for me?
reference_answer: Yes. LPU's examination code lets students with a permanent or temporary disability use a writer or scribe.

question: The library doesn't have a book I need. Can it get it from another library?
reference_answer: Yes. LPU's libraries offer Inter-Library Loan through DELNET, New Delhi. Requests for books and articles go by email to central.library@lpu.co.in with the author, title, publisher, year and edition.

question: Who is on the committee that handles sexual harassment complaints?
reference_answer: The Internal Complaints Committee, constituted by the Registrar: a Presiding Officer who is a senior woman faculty member, two faculty members and two non-teaching staff members, one member from an NGO or a person familiar with sexual harassment issues, and three students if the matter involves students.

question: can i bring my smartwatch to the end term exam
reference_answer: No. Smart watches are prohibited items and are not even allowed inside the examination venue. Being found with one leads to an Unfair Means Case (UMC) and cancellation of further scholarship.

question: I'm going to be 40 minutes late for my exam, will they still let me in?
reference_answer: Candidates must be seated 30 minutes before the exam starts. A candidate who is more than 30 minutes late from the reporting time because of unavoidable circumstances may be allowed to appear provisionally, with written approval from the centre superintendent.

question: Can I carry a water bottle into the exam room?
reference_answer: Yes, but only drinking water in a clear, unlabelled bottle or container.

question: There was a mistake in my question paper. How do I complain about it online, and is there a deadline?
reference_answer: Within 72 hours of the scheduled exam, through UMS Navigation > Examination. Several discrepancies can be entered for the same course.

question: What is the maximum attendance shortage that can be condoned in a term?
reference_answer: Up to 10% in a term. How much is condoned depends on the student's aggregate attendance in the two previous terms, according to the condonation table.

question: Are jeans allowed under the dress code?
reference_answer: No. Jeans are not allowed; only formal trousers are permitted.

question: I lost my migration certificate. How do I get a new one and what does it cost?
reference_answer: Rs 500, with an affidavit signed before a first-class magistrate declaring that the original was lost and has not been used to seek admission anywhere.

question: till what time is the main library open on sundays
reference_answer: The Central LPU Library is open from 8:00 am to 12:00 midnight every day, including Sundays and holidays. The other block libraries open from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Saturday.

question: How many books can I borrow from the library at once and for how long?
reference_answer: A regular student can borrow up to 3 books at a time for up to one week (part-time students get 15 days). Students in honours courses can borrow 5 books for 15 days.

question: What time do I have to be back in my hostel room in December?
reference_answer: From 1 November to 28 February, evening hostel attendance is at 7:00 PM. It is at 8:00 PM from 1 May to 31 October and at 7:30 PM from 1 March to 30 April.

question: Can I extend my hostel leave if I'm running late, and how many times?
reference_answer: Yes. An extended day or night leave adds up to 3 hours to an existing leave in unavoidable circumstances. Extensions can be used at most 8 times a month, with 30 per category in each academic term.

question: I'm a fresher. How do I ask for a refund of my hostel fee?
reference_answer: Freshers apply by email to refund@lpu.co.in from their registered email ID. The date the email is received counts as the date of the refund application.

question: Can I switch my branch after first year, and can I do it twice?
reference_answer: Only in exceptional circumstances and with approval. The request is made online on UMS with the parent's consent letter, and the program can be changed only once during the entire program.

question: What CGPA do I need to opt for credit transfer abroad?
reference_answer: Continuing students need at least 6.5 CGPA with no backlogs or reappears, no indiscipline case, and at least one year spent at LPU. Freshmen need 65% in the lower qualifying exam. A partner university may ask for more.

question: What is a Discipline Minor elective?
reference_answer: A set of four elective courses in one area that builds a competency outside the student's major area.

question: Where do I collect my academic certificates on campus?
reference_answer: From Block 32, Room 101, on any working day, after applying on UMS (Examination > Certificate Request). Someone else can collect them with an authority letter and ID proofs of both the student and that person.

question: Do I have to clear my backlogs to keep my placement offer?
reference_answer: Yes. All pending reappears and backlogs must be cleared by the end of the final semester, otherwise the placement offer may be revoked because the degree could be extended.

question: What is the late fee if I pay my spring term fee on 15 January 2027?
reference_answer: Rs 1,000. The late fee for payments from 11 to 20 January 2027 is Rs 1,000; there is no late fee up to 31 December 2026.

question: I was on DL for a sports event and missed all my CAs. How will I get marks for them?
reference_answer: The CA is prorated from the student's marks in the mid term exam (MTE) of that course. For example, 60 out of 80 in the MTE gives prorated CA marks of 75 out of 100.

question: I paid my fee three days ago but it isn't showing on UMS. What should I do, and what happens if it never shows up?
reference_answer: If the fee is not reflected within 3 working days, submit the details at UMS > Finance Management System > Fee Dashboard > Confirmation of Fee Deposited. If the fee is not paid or not reflected, the student is not registered for the next term and cannot attend classes, and attendance stays blocked until the fee is cleared; paying the late fee later gives no claim for that loss.

question: Can I use a pen during answer sheet scrutiny for the MTT or the ETE?
reference_answer: No, in both cases. Only a lead pencil may be used during MTT and ETE scrutiny; a student found with any kind of pen is treated as an Unfair Means case.

question: I'm on duty leave for a placement drive. What happens if I miss my MTE, and what if I miss the ETE?
reference_answer: A mid term exam missed on duty leave is prorated from the marks in the end term exam, if the student sits the ETE. A missed ETE or ETP is not prorated: the student takes it on a new schedule set by the Division of Examination, without any fee.

question: Can I use my phone in the library? And can I keep it in my bag during the end term exam?
reference_answer: No to both. Using a mobile phone in the library is strictly prohibited and phones must be on silent or switched off. Mobile phones are prohibited items in the end term exam and are not even allowed inside the venue; being found with one leads to an Unfair Means Case.

question: What attendance do I need to sit the ETE, and how is my attendance counted if I changed my program after classes started?
reference_answer: At least 75% aggregate attendance after the 5% relaxation, with at least 65% in each course. After a program change once classes have started, attendance is counted from the start of classes or the last date of admission, whichever is later: days before registration in the new program count as absent, and lectures attended in the old program are carried over.

question: What passport do I need for a semester abroad, and for the credit transfer option?
reference_answer: For a semester or year abroad, the passport must remain valid for at least six months beyond the period applied for. For credit transfer, the student needs a valid passport before the application process starts.

question: If an international student withdraws on 20 August 2026, is the admission processing fee refunded, and are application or late fees refundable?
reference_answer: No. The admission processing fee is not refunded from 16 to 30 August 2026 (or 21 to 30 days after admission, whichever is later). Prospectus, application, processing, entrance, late, programme transfer and migration fees are non-refundable in all circumstances unless stated otherwise.

question: What academic benefit do I get for a 25 LPA placement, and until when can I apply for it?
reference_answer: A placement above 20 and up to 30 LPA (category Z(D)) gives a 2-level grade upgrade in 3 courses, if the student scores at least 40% in the ETT. The benefit can be applied for until 31 May of the passing-out year.

question: How long does a PhD take at minimum, and how many external experts evaluate the thesis?
reference_answer: At least three years from registration (at most six). The thesis is evaluated by at least two external experts.

question: Which places does the LPU bus come from, and can day scholars park on campus?
reference_answer: Buses run from Amritsar, Ludhiana, Hoshiarpur, Mukerian, Kapurthala, Jalandhar and Nawanshahr (non-AC except Ludhiana). Parking is available to day scholars as well as residents.
